title: Grade 6 Science — Wed, Jun 11
description: Separation of Substances — Day 3 of 5: Evaporation and distillation
subject: science

questions.question: Evaporation is used to separate a ____ substance from its solution.
questions.explanation: Evaporation is used when a solid is dissolved in a liquid. Heating removes the liquid as vapour, leaving the solid.

questions.question: Salt is obtained from seawater by:
questions.explanation: In salt pans along India's coasts, seawater is allowed to evaporate in sun and wind, leaving behind salt crystals.

questions.question: During evaporation of saltwater, what happens to the water?
options: It turns into water vapour and escapes
questions.explanation: When salt solution is heated, water evaporates (turns to vapour and escapes), leaving solid salt behind.

questions.question: Evaporation is NOT suitable for separating:
options: Alcohol from water (heat would destroy both)
questions.explanation: If both substances have similar boiling points or we want to collect both, distillation is used instead of evaporation.

questions.question: Distillation is used to separate:
options: Two liquids with different boiling points
questions.explanation: Distillation separates two liquids that have different boiling points — the more volatile one evaporates first and is collected.

questions.question: In distillation, the vapour is cooled in a condenser and collected as:
questions.explanation: The vapour rises, passes through a cooled condenser, turns back to liquid (distillate), and is collected in a flask.

questions.question: Pure (distilled) water is obtained from seawater by:
questions.explanation: Distillation of seawater produces pure distilled water by evaporating and condensing water vapour, leaving salts behind.

questions.question: The boiling point of water is ____ and ethanol is 78 °C. Distillation separates them by:
options: 100 °C; heating just above 78 °C so only ethanol boils first
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C, ethanol at 78 °C. Heating to ~80 °C causes ethanol to vaporise first and be collected separately.

questions.question: Coastal states like Gujarat use vast salt pans. The energy used to evaporate seawater is:
questions.explanation: India's salt pans use free solar energy — sunlight heats shallow seawater, causing water to evaporate and leaving salt.

questions.question: The process of a liquid changing to vapour on heating is called:
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour (gas). It occurs at the surface of the liquid.

questions.question: The process of vapour changing back to liquid on cooling is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change from vapour (gas) to liquid on cooling. Distillation uses condensation to collect the separated liquid.

questions.question: Which method would you use to get clean water from muddy salt water in one step?
questions.explanation: Distillation removes both mud and dissolved salt — water evaporates and is condensed, leaving impurities behind.

questions.question: In the fractional distillation of crude oil, different fuels separate because they have:
questions.explanation: Different components of crude oil (petrol, kerosene, diesel) boil at different temperatures, separating them by distillation.

questions.question: Why does evaporation happen faster on a hot, windy day?
options: Higher temperature and wind increase evaporation rate
questions.explanation: Higher temperature gives liquid molecules more energy to escape, and wind carries vapour away — both increase evaporation rate.

questions.question: Sugar solution is heated until all the water evaporates. What will you find in the dish?
questions.explanation: Sugar has a very high boiling point and does not evaporate easily. Heating removes only the water, leaving solid sugar.
